html:
GIMM-VFI (GIMM-VFI-R and its perceptual GIMM-VFI-R-P, Guo et al., NeurIPS 2024): makes the frame at any time between two video frames from a learned continuous motion field (RAFT flow), for slow motion and higher frame rates. Non-commercial code and weights (S-Lab License 1.0).

Commercial use: no (code: LicenseRef-noncommercial (noncommercial); weights: LicenseRef-noncommercial).

Details
  • Original code: https://github.com/GSeanCDAT/GIMM-VFI at dbc56449994a
  • Code licence: LicenseRef-noncommercial (noncommercial); files: LICENSE
  • Weights licence: LicenseRef-noncommercial
  • Licence evidence: https://github.com/GSeanCDAT/GIMM-VFI/blob/dbc56449994a3c2e045d46fd46bed570239913f8/LICENSE ; https://github.com/GSeanCDAT/GIMM-VFI/blob/dbc56449994a3c2e045d46fd46bed570239913f8/README.md (weights: https://huggingface.co/GSean/GIMM-VFI)
  • Training data: Vimeo-90K (septuplets / triplets for frame interpolation) (configs/gimmvfi/gimmvfi_r_arb.yaml: Vimeo-90K septuplets with arbitrary-time targets; the RAFT flow estimator starts from the raft-things checkpoint (FlyingChairs + FlyingThings3D).)
  • Kernel libraries: raft_flow, cudnn_hacc
  • Variants: gimm-vfi-r, gimm-vfi-r-p
  • Outputs: frame
  • Input size: any H x W >= 128, padded to a multiple of 32
  • Tested up to (portable, fp16, RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB): gimm-vfi-r 1024x2048 (13.4 GiB peak allocated, 14.5 reserved); gimm-vfi-r-p 1024x2048 (13.0 GiB peak allocated, 14.2 reserved)
  • gimm-vfi-r 1080x1920, first call: portable + torch.compile 307 s (cold Inductor cache).
  • gimm-vfi-r-p 1080x1920, first call: portable + torch.compile 307 s (cold Inductor cache).
  • gimm-vfi-r load / first call: original 2.05 s / 1.336 s (480x854), portable 0.27 s / 2.622 s, kernels 0.59 s / 1.631 s
  • gimm-vfi-r-p load / first call: original 2.96 s / 1.438 s (480x854), portable 0.27 s / 0.997 s (480x854), kernels 0.58 s / 0.684 s (480x854)
  • Protocol, first call, 3 warm-up, peak reset, median of 3 rounds x median of 5

Measured

DAVIS 2017 trainval 480p (JPEG), frames 0 / 2 and 20 / 22 of each of the 90 videos give the frame 1 / 21 at time 0.5, compared with the real one: PSNR and SSIM (Gaussian 11 x 11, sigma 1.5) of the output rounded to uint8, on RGB in [0, 1], averaged over the triplets. Original = the original code named under Details, same checkpoint and protocol.

Parity

CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 5e-05 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.0003 and p99 <= 0.003 (absolute error of the output frame).
